solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Trouble with hothead idiot, the French …

parts.note: the head of the word hot, its first letter, is H
an ass is a fool
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Trouble brewing with a hot-headed fool, and a Frenchman at that, trailing off.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis ties this clue to the next one in surface only; 'hothead' is read as the head of 'hot'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester or harass someone is to cause them bother, and the noun names annoying bother.

clue.text: Repeal brought up in jail, unnaturally

indicators.note: brought up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something is raised in prison in an odd way, then withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'brought up' reads the letters bottom to top; the hidden run is LUNNA.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke or cancel it officially.

clue.text: Captained ship opening with preserved fish

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word

parts.note: kippered fish, like herring, has been split, salted and smoked

explanation.surface: A captain begins a voyage with a hold of cured herrings.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is a captain, so to have skippered a vessel is to have commanded it.

clue.text: Government of European politician facing anger

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A Continental member of parliament faces public fury over his rule.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a realm under one supreme authority, a form of rule or dominion.

clue.text: … expose a French wally — the conclusion's explosive

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article, a
a wally and a clot are both British slang for a fool
HE is the abbreviation for high explosive

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: a French fool gets exposed, and the ending blows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the conclusion's explosive' says the final piece is HE, high explosive. Wally is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip someone of their garments lays the body bare, so it is a synonym of expose.

clue.text: Rough seduction is path to clash

indicators.note: clash says the letters collide into a jumbled new order

explanation.surface: A crude seducer's approach leads only to conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough in the sense of crude and unrefined, lacking worldly polish.

clue.text: Cooking fish round centre of griddle

indicators.note: round says one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: a codling is a young cod

indicators.note: centre of means the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: Frying fish around the middle of a hot plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of the seven-letter GRIDDLE is D, which goes inside CODLING.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle eggs is to cook them gently in water just below boiling.

clue.text: Former blonde seen topless

indicators.note: topless means the top letter, the first in a down entry, is removed

parts.note: golden hair is blonde hair

explanation.surface: An ex-partner, a fair-haired woman, spotted without a top.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden means of bygone days, belonging to times past.

clue.text: Reservation at Chinese buffet

indicators.note: to buffet is to knock about, so the letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: A table booked at a Chinese self-service restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' poses as a meal but is a verb, knock about.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservation is a doubt or reluctance, which is hesitation.

clue.text: Hip set admitting woman's laid up

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: something hip is in, fashionable
set, as in placed or arranged, can mean posed
Di is a woman's name, and with the 's it gives DIS

explanation.surface: A trendy group lets in a woman who is bedridden.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone laid up is ill and confined to bed, which is being unwell or out of sorts.

clue.text: Fly speck

definitions.meaning: to fly is to rush off quickly, to hurry away
a speck is a tiny amount, as in a small splash of milk

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a sudden rush or hurry, and a small quantity added to something.

clue.text: Cold course ingredient's flipping tripe!

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a lap is one circuit of a race course

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an ingredient is a part of a mixture

explanation.surface: A diner exclaims that an item in a cold dish is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reads like a mild British oath attached to the exclamation, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe in the slang sense is worthless nonsense, empty pretentious talk.

clue.text: Term of Liberal and then changes around Government

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters are wrapped about the next piece
changes says the letters of then are rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician's period in office, during which the government reshuffles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' turns THEN into ENTH, and 'around' puts that round G to give ENGTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a period of time, and its duration is how long it lasts.

clue.text: English border turned back foreign leader

indicators.note: turned back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: An overseas ruler was turned away at the English frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or prince, a commander in the Arab world.

clue.text: Wreck created involving a large jam

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or wreck

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: made means created
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: A big traffic snarl-up caused by a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' looks like a traffic hold-up; it is a preserve, as in orange jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus preserve, a kind of jam made from oranges.

clue.text: Not intelligent from design, or anthropology

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Dismissing someone as dim on the evidence of their design or anthropology work.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking knowledge or education makes one uninformed, loosely unintelligent.

clue.text: Provoking hatred, pure evil's let loose

indicators.note: let loose says the letters are freed and rearranged

parts.note: the s of evil's is kept as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Pure evil is unleashed and stirs up loathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repellent arouses disgust and loathing in those who see it.

clue.text: Fabulous wife's shut up and run off

parts.note: to pen an animal is to shut it up in an enclosure
to elope is to run off secretly to marry

explanation.surface: A gossip says the marvellous wife has been locked away and fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means of fable: in Greek legend Odysseus's faithful wife waited twenty years for him.
explanation.definitionFit: The loyal wife of Odysseus in Homer's legendary Odyssey, a figure of fable.

clue.text: Bank in danger, it turned out

indicators.note: turned out means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A bank in trouble, and so it proved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' wants to be a financial one; it is a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of earth is a slope, and a slope's steepness is its incline.

clue.text: Gander is run over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to run a shop is to keep it

explanation.surface: A goose is knocked down by a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gander' looks like the goose; it is British slang for a look, as in 'have a gander'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a gander is taking a quick look, a glance or peep.

clue.text: Bloody, getting sewn up

definitions.meaning: a mild euphemistic oath, as in 'a blasted nuisance'
mended with stitching, as socks with a hole

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a softened curse word, and repaired with needle and thread.

clue.text: Staff get on to command

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it
to get on is to grow older, to age

explanation.surface: Employees climb the ladder to reach a position of command.
explanation.definitionFit: To command an enterprise is to run or direct it, which is to be in charge.

clue.text: Mac endlessly concealing a shock

indicators.note: concealing means hiding one piece inside the other
endlessly says the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a Mac is a computer made by Apple

explanation.surface: A man named Mac endlessly hides a shocking secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify or dismay, to give a nasty jolt.

clue.text: Restrained following 'Tea, vicar?'

indicators.note: following says this piece comes after the other one

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
plain means simple and restrained, without ornament

explanation.surface: Someone holds back after being offered tea by the vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vicar' sits as the addressee in the offer of tea, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman serving an institution such as a hospital or regiment; loosely any cleric.

clue.text: Initially indolent dosser liking endless rest

definitions.text: Initially indolent dosser liking endless rest

indicators.note: initially says take the first letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: A lazy layabout who loves never-ending repose.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a lazy loafer who loves to lie about doing nothing.

clue.text: Talk quietly and breathe with difficulty

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone murmurs and is short of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: To pant or draw a sudden short breath is to struggle for air.

clue.text: Seeming to be less 'in' somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Apparently, being less fashionable just happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent, outwardly so but perhaps not really so, which is how something seems.

clue.text: Start of spring?

parts.note: read not as the season's beginning but as the source where spring water rises

explanation.definitionFit: A wellhead is the place where a spring rises from the ground, its source.

clue.text: Flat bottom in display case

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
case means the outer letters, the casing, of the word

parts.note: the rear is the backside, the bottom

explanation.surface: A dull exhibit with a backside in a glass cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat in the sense of dull and lifeless, lacking interest or spirit.
